2026 SEMA Show • Ford Frostwarden, a Bronco SUV With Over 1,200 HP, the R125 and F-250 Also in Tow
New Hot Wheels Ferrari 80th Anniversary Multipack Looks Better Than I Originally Thought
14 photos
Photo: Ministry of Diecast
Oh the weather outside is awful! I haven’t seen the sun in several days now, and it looks like my village is about to be hit by a blizzard tomorrow. That means I can’t proceed with my first Hot Wheels unboxing for November, as there just isn’t enough light for some nice shots.
I also don’t want to fully rely on my Miami-themed diorama for the job, so I’ll have to find a different solution. Meanwhile, Mattel just publicly announced the Racer Series today, which means we finally have more accurate photos of the six cars.
According to the official website, the manufacturer is betting on a “Blind Purchase” strategy which means you will get a random model with each order. That’s one way to deal with both scalpers and peg-warmers in one shot.
We will have to wait a while longer until the pricing is revealed, so let’s focus on something else for the time being. The Ferrari 80th Anniversary 5-Pack didn’t come as a surprise, as we’ve already seen teasers for it since August.
In the image that was circulating online at the time, all five cars were red, though. And the F355 Berlinetta was still in a ZAMAC phase, using Real Riders wheels. Let me walk you through the whole thing.
SF90 Stradale Photo: Ministry of Diecast The SF90 Stradale is first in line, and you might remember it debuted last year in the Factory Fresh mini-series. It was one of three brand new Ferrari Mainline castings, alongside the F40 Competizione and the 365 GTB4 Competizione.
And if you think about it, it was also only one of four modern Ferraris Mattel revealed in 2025. We had two versions of the 499P plus the RC take on the SF90 Stradale Assetto Fiorano, while all the other castings were replicas of older Italian machines.
This SF90 has had seven variations so far, all while going through four different wheel designs. The original impression was that Rosso Corsa would be the manufacturer’s go-to option for the Anniversary release.
However, it now seems we’ll be able to get a Blanco Avus variation of the supercar. Depending on how old you are, it might be the least desirable collectible in the set, though.
Testarossa Photo: Ministry of Diecast There’s a good chance everyone will want a piece of the Testarossa, as this is the casting’s second variation so far. You can still get these in the real world for less than $200,000, as its value hasn’t skyrocketed like we’ve seen with cars like the F50. I know they’re on two completely different levels, and that $200,000 is still a budget most working-class citizens can’t afford.
However, you can still dream about it, which has to count for something, right? Ronald Wong designed the casting for this year’s Car Culture: Modern Classics set and I was lucky enough to find it in a grocery store of all places.
Seeing it as a Silver Series release doesn’t mean it will automatically have a Mainline variation next, as Mattel would probably even consider creating a new casting based on a different trim for that purpose alone. I’m sure something like a Testarossa Spider would start a treasure hunt, so it might be an option for either Elite 64 or the Red Line Club instead.
If you know anything about my taste in tiny cars then it shouldn’t surprise you that I’m a huge fan of the S5 wheels on this collectible. They’re not as exciting as the Real Riders Exotics, but we should also think of the price difference. As far as I can tell, the Testarossa will be the only car in this set to feature a metal base, so there’s one more reason for you to find one soon.
812 Superfast Photo: Ministry of Diecast The Ferrari 812 Superfast is the first brand-new casting in this multipack, and it’s Ronald Wong’s creation. What a surprise! It’s one of five Ferraris he has created for 2027, and there are about eight more of them that showed up in 2025 and 2026.
We already know that the model’s successor, the 12Cilindri, is getting a Super Treasure Hunt release next year. Knowing that the 812 Superfast is one its way gives me hope that Mattel should be releasing the F12 or F12 TDF sometime within the next 24 months, too.
I can already see how the three of them together could show up in an exclusive V12-themed set, maybe alongside the 599 GTO and the 575M Maranello. It’s almost unthinkable that it won’t happen, just as it’s unthinkable not to have a GTO, F40, F50, Enzo and LaFerrari mix at some point.
Anyway, I’m daydreaming here, and I confess it’s unexpected to see the 812 Superfast making its debut sporting a Grigio Silverstone finish. It’s still better than having another red car again, don’t get me wrong! And I’m glad to see the yellow stripes running down the middle for some contrast.
F355 Berlinetta Photo: Ministry of Diecast Seeing this tiny version of the F355 Berlinetta after having driven in in Gran Turismo 7 for dozens of laps recently is a funny coincidence. I’m sure there’s no connection between the two events whatsoever, even though the timing makes it seem like it.
Of course we have Mr. Wong to thank for this casting too, and I’d say it’s quite a bold decision to release it Nero Daytona. If it loses the top it could easily serve as a Fast and Furious collectible next.
This car is obviously not as popular as Rosso Corsa but I’m sure more of them came out of the factory with it than they did in Azzuro Dino or Verde Mugello. There’s a good chance the team in El Segundo already knows what the next variation will look like, and we’ll just have to wait and see how it turns out.
Call me crazy if you will, bu I’d say this is the most desirable car in the set, as I already have a Testarossa and don’t really care about the other three ones as much.
365 GTB4 Competizione Photo: Ministry of Diecast Don’t get me wrong, the 365 GTB4 Competizione looks great in Blu Dino! It’s hand down the best variation so far if only for that reason, and we’ve had five of them by now. I unboxed the First Edition release a while ago, and have mostly ignored it since.
Switching from the 5-Spoke rims to the Retro Slot Wheels wasn’t an improvement, whereas the Star 5-Spoke, Silver Series design is a step in the right direction. I realize not every Hot Wheels Ferrari casting can become a premium model but you have to ask the question: is this 365 GTB4 Competizione “doomed” to be stuck in the entry-level categories forever?
There’s still some potential in Pop Culture with a Miami Vice replica, even it means “downgrading” to a regular Daytona. I have a feeling this multipack won’t become a peg-warmer like the basic 5-pack that you can still see in toy stores all over right now.
Even though pre-orders with some dealers started back in August, I hope there will be plenty of them to go around in a few weeks time. I got word of the launch from my buddy Zali from Ministry of Diecast, who pointed out that you can already buy the set from Rakuten in Japan. Will you be going after it, too?

The King Tide Is an Aussie-Built Camper Van That Swaps the Rear Bed for a Massive Beach Mode Lounge
23 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia
Australia is one of the go-to places for van lifers due to the vast wilderness and rough but beautiful environments. There are many companies to choose from when it comes to building or buying a camper van. One of them is Summit Vans – today, I'm checking out its latest conversion.
Meet King Tide, a conversion based on a 2026 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase, finished in Stone Grey paint. Its creator, Summit Vans, is a Wollongong, Australia-based company specializing in premium, Sprinter-based camper van conversions.
As usual, let's first take a look at the exterior. The vehicle rides on Reika wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires. You can pretty much tell as soon as you lay eyes on the vehicle that it's a mobile home.
The van has a GVM suspension upgrade, with upgraded leaf springs and an upper rear shock reinforcement. This setup increases the GVM from 4,100 kg (9,039 lb.) to 4,430 kg (9,766 lb.). Summit Vans went even further and installed a Van Compass suspension kit with front and rear Falcon adjustable shocks.
At the rear, you'll come across a Weldbeat spare tire carrier/ladder combo next to another carrier holding a cargo box. Climb on the roof, and you'll discover a Wedgetail rack holding a Fiamma awning, a flat-mounted Starlink antenna, and a 200 W solar array.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Other notable mods are Weldbeat full-length side steps, power and water hookups, and awning-style bunk windows on the sides.
Stepping inside, you'll be greeted by a bright and beautiful interior. A key detail is that it has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
The driver and passenger seats are mounted on factory swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and be used after you set up camp.
Regarding design, the customer opted for white laminated cabinetry, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, walls upholstered with grey woven fabric, and a bamboo slatted ceiling with recessed LED light strips. The look is complemented by a variety of black accents, such as the cabinet or drawer handles, and bamboo countertops.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Normally, most customers opt for a seating area straight ahead of the entrance. However, this customer chose to have some extra kitchen and storage space. Specifically, they requested a counter complete with a large cabinet and a drawer. It also offers a decently sized top with additional meal prep space and charging points.
Above are two cabinets – one of them houses the rig's "command center." It includes a touchscreen display that lets you monitor and control the power system, three dimmer light switches, and various switches for the water pump, Wi-Fi, and more.
Next, we have a floor-to-ceiling unit on the same side. It integrates a microwave oven, an overhead cabinet with a plug, and a huge fridge with a freezer compartment.
The primary kitchen unit sits on the passenger side, beside the entrance. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cover and a portable induction stove. Two overhead shelves, four drawers, a pull-out pantry, and three lower cabinets are available for storage.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia On the opposite side, Summit Vans devised one of the most sought-after camper van facilities: the bathroom. It boasts a shower with a handheld wand, an OGO Nomad toilet, and a vent that draws out the moisture outside. Moreover, you can use a wall-mounted L-Track to attach a small clothesline or other gear.
The rear part of the interior is where you'll find the van's stand-out features: Summit Vans' innovative Beach Mode rear lounge and garage configuration. You'll also notice L-Tracks on the side walls that hold two Sirocco fans, a Maxxair vent fan above, and four overhead cabinets.
Instead of a traditional fixed rear bed, the company created a massive lounge area with a Lagun table and a U-shaped couch that can be turned into a king-size bed. If for any reason you don't want to do that, you can still use the benches on the sides as two single beds.
To turn the area into a sleeping arrangement, you must remove the Lagun table and use its top, along with several extra panels, to connect the benches. Then, rearrange the cushions, and the result is an almost king-size bed. Specifically, it measures 170 centimeters (67 inches) in width and 195 centimeters (76 inches) in length.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia The benches also accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the passenger side – the electrical system's highlights are an 820 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. You can use three charging sources to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 180-liter (47-gallon) freshwater tank inside the driver-side bench, an under-mounted 45-liter (12-gallon) greywater tank, a water filtration system, and an electric water heater.
There is one more surprise at the back of the van: an abundance of storage space. Open the rear doors, and you'll discover two surprisingly long and roomy drawers, as well as a small cabinet and a smaller drawer.
So, this Beach Mode not only cleverly uses the space for seating and sleeping, but also leaves a bunch of room for storage in the garage accessible from the back of the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia All in all, King Tide perfectly showcases Summit Vans' expertise in transforming vans into homes on wheels. Thanks to the Beach Mode feature, this camper van packs a flexible space without compromising adventure capability.

1963 Chevrolet Sitting on a Trailer Beg for Restoration if You Don't Get Scared Easily
17 photos
Photo: eBay seller lamonte6447
1963 is the year, and rough is the term that describes it best. This 1963 Chevrolet Impala is here because it’s dreaming about the same thing as many other abandoned classics.
The car needs a complete restoration, but before anything else, it must convince an Internet stranger to take it home. That’s why the owner posted it on eBay, where the car should sell by this time next month.
The owner doesn’t reveal many specifics about this 1963 Chevrolet, probably hoping that the photos in the gallery tell the whole story. At some level, they do, but they also leave many questions without an answer.
Photo: eBay seller lamonte6447 1963 was such a fantastic year for Chevrolet , and the sales recorded by the company speak for themselves. The GM brand sold no more, no less than 1.57 million full-size cars, and the Impala accounted for over 50% of this number. Over 832,000 Chevrolet buyers ordered an Impala, and the best thing about this number was that the V8 engines accounted for an impressive number.
More than 735,000 Impalas left the factory with a V8 engine, and eventually, V8 power represented over 1.1 million Chevrolets sold this year.
The increased demand for V8 engines made sense, especially because the Super Sport was becoming a more popular name in the Chevrolet lineup. Only 153,000 Impalas rolled off the assembly line with the SS package.
Chevrolet continued to focus on a mix of engines that included both six-cylinder units and V8s power. The base choice was a 230ci unit with 140 horsepower, while the foray into the V8 lineup started with a 283 Turbo-Fire rated at 195 horsepower.
A 327 small-block configuration rated at 250 horsepower was a very popular choice, but customers who didn’t want to stick with this setup and wanted more power could get an upgraded version that was fitted with solid lifters and which developed 340 horsepower.
The top choice was a 409 big-block engine that produced 400 or 425 horsepower. Chevrolet also offered the Z11 drag pack package, which was rated at over 500 horsepower and carried a super-hefty price tag of $1,245. It included dual four-barrel carburetors, dual exhausts, high-lift cams, solid lifters, and an impressive 13.5:1 compression ratio.
Photo: eBay seller lamonte6447 This Impala isn’t as impressive as a Z11-powered specimen, but on the plus side, it still seems to have an engine under the hood.
This means it might still be in good mechanical shape, but considering the owner did not include any other specifics in their listing, the only option is to call them and ask all these questions. It looks to be a 327, but no other details are available, so it’s unclear if this is the original unit.
If it is, I wouldn’t expect it to be working, though a good mechanic should be able to decrypt the full story with a quick inspection.
Other than that, you don’t have to be a diehard restoration guy to figure out the rest of the details. The thick layer of dust suggests this Impala has recently been pulled from storage, while the rust and the huge floors that let clean air come through indicate that it has probably spent more than just a few years in the same place.
This could be a barn find pulled after decades, and that’s why it’s such a shame that the owner did not include additional details and maybe more detailed photos.
Photo: eBay seller lamonte6447 While some parts are obviously required, including a gas tank, the car looks fairly complete. Obviously, not everything is in condition that would allow a restoration guy to retain them after the full refresh, but on the plus side, you won’t spend countless hours online looking for parts.
It’s pretty clear that restoring this Impala won’t be easy, and I think that you need a good metal guy to fix those massive holes before anything else.
It’s time to talk money, as this is one of the most important things about a rough Chevrolet whose long-term objective is to return to the road one day.
Photo: eBay seller lamonte6447 The owner listed the car with a $6,300 price tag, but they also enabled the Make Offer option. This is typically a good sign, as it’s an indication that the owner is open to other offers, so you can use this button if you’re interested in the car but have another deal in mind.
I still recommend that potential buyers call the seller and arrange an in-person inspection, especially as all the details are missing. The vehicle is parked in Los Angeles, and you should also consider shipping costs, considering the overall condition of the car.
The listing expires in four weeks, and this is great news for every possible buyer, as this means they’re getting enough time to obtain all the information they need to make an informed decision.
Via // eBay

This 1971 Dodge Challenger R/T Lost Its Original Engine but There's No Reason To Be Upset
27 photos
Photo: eBay seller mrsvator4u
It’s hard not to like a real-deal Challenger R/T, even if you’re not a Dodge fan. That’s why this specimen is very likely to catch the attention of many people online, as it’s a genuine R/T - true R/T, not a clone, as the owner explains - wearing a beautiful color.
This Challenger R/T is here because it started the sometimes long and very difficult search for a new home. It’s finished in the fantastic Hemi Orange and sports the R/T stripes, with a fiberglass hood and a Shaker design.
This car is no longer original, but I don’t think that’s a big problem this time. I mean, yes, an all-original Challenger R/T would have been significantly better, but considering this car received a massive upgrade, it’s hard to be upset about this decision.
Photo: eBay seller mrsvator4u The “new” American car market was less about the performance hiding under the hood and more about efficiency and economy. With insurance costs also rising, more and more buyers decided to look for smaller engines, and models like the GTO and the Challenger suffered.
Dodge recorded another decline, and the Challenger dropped from over 83,000 cars sold in 1970 to fewer than 30,000 units. On the good side, most people who bought a Challenger ended up picking a V8 engine, despite Dodge still offering a slant six.
Oddly, despite six-cylinder engines making more sense than ever given the new trends, Challenger buyers didn’t like the idea of fitting a car whose main selling point was the muscle under the hood with a lazy engine. The six-cylinder-powered Challenger was also the most affordable in the entire lineup, carrying a price of $2,858.
Photo: eBay seller mrsvator4u The base V8 was a 318 that could be had for $2,853, but Dodge also offered more powerful engines, beginning with a 340 rated at 275 horsepower and available for $253. The 383 was the most popular choice with 300 horsepower, while the 440 Six-Pack allowed buyers to step into the big-block world for $460.
The Hemi continued to be available with 425 horsepower, but considering it carried a price tag of no more, no less than $790, few customers ended up getting it.
Some popular options continued to be offered at premium prices. For example, air conditioning could be installed on any Challenger for $374.
Photo: eBay seller mrsvator4u This Challenger was born with a 340 four-barrel engine, but it’s now fitted with a big-block 440 with fuel injection. The engine has already been rebuilt, and the seller explains on eBay that the odometer shows only 850 miles since it was rebuilt.
The engine is paired with a 4-speed manual transmission with a pistol-grip shifter. An aluminum radiator and an electric fan have also been installed, and the vehicle has been converted to four-wheel manual disc brakes for extra stopping power.
Needless to say, everything starts, runs, and drives properly. This Challenger appears to be in very good shape, but I still recommend that every buyer, even a little interested in this car, call the seller and arrange an in-person inspection. This is the best way to determine if the Challenger is worth the money because I can assure you that the car isn’t affordable.
Before I reveal the price, there’s something else I want to highlight.
This Challenger R/T is no longer original, and the new engine, the upgraded brakes, and the new radiator are living proof that the dream of an all-original Challenger has faded away on this car. But on the other hand, the seller says several other original parts continue to be available, even if they are no longer installed in the car.
Photo: eBay seller mrsvator4u For example, the buyer will get the original factory metal bumpers, the original factory radio and antenna, as well as the windshield wipers. The engine is no longer available.
I think this is a no-brainer, but a 1971 Challenger R/T in this condition and with upgraded power under the hood can’t be cheap. This specimen really isn’t, but on the other hand, it doesn’t get too close to those siblings that continue to be entirely original and are fitted with massive engines under the hood.
The upgrades and the lack of any documentation have taken their toll on the price, so this Challenger R/T can be yours for $52,500. The seller has also enabled the Make Offer option, so with a little luck and the right negotiation skills, you might be able to get a better deal if you are committed to a purchase.
The listing will expire in 10 days, but with 49 people already watching the car, there’s hope that someone will eventually take it home. The car is parked in Dubuque, Iowa, and it should be able to travel to your garage after the purchase without you needing to cover the extra costs of shipping if you’re the adventurous type.
Via // eBay

2026 SEMA Show • Ringbrothers Mesmerizes the SEMA Show Once Again, This Time With Billie, the 650-HP Pontiac GTO
One-of-None 1970 Hemi Challenger Rocks Coolest Dealer-Installed Accessory, Two Owners in 56 Years
91 photos
Photo: YouTube/DezzysSpeedShop
Back in 1969, Detroit engineers apparently substituted their morning coffee with high-octane leaded fumes, looked at a brick-shaped coupe, hammered a towering stabilizer onto the trunk, and declared war on physics. That glorious corporate fever dream birthed the winged aero warriors that every collector worships today, the fabulous Charger Daytona (and its subsequent sibling, the 1970 Plymouth Road Runner Superbird). Yet someone in California wanted a 1970 Dodge Challenger R/T 426 Hemi with a genuine Charger Daytona wing right from the dealership showroom floor. And he got it.
Before purists faint into their restoration manuals, let us state the obvious: Dodge never offered a towering wing on the Challenger, making this machine a glorious one-of-zero anomaly. In fact, no American pony car ever received a skyscraper stabilizer from the factory, as Detroit reserved such aerodynamic lunacy strictly for intermediate B-body racers from Ma Mopar. Yet when Troy Bergeron of the Mopars5150 YouTube channel examined this coupe, its wild past proved undeniable.
Understanding how a towering aluminum clothesline ended up on an E-body requires revisiting 1969, when Dodge unleashed the Charger Daytona for just one model year to conquer NASCAR ovals. Realizing that standard Chargers possessed the aerodynamic efficiency of a flying sack of bricks near 200 mph (322 kph), Chrysler summoned its aerospace division brainiacs.
Rocket scientists grafted on a pointy nose cone (hey, a missile needs to be pointy to look mean, right?) and a 23-inch (584-millimeter) rear wing that reached clean, undisturbed air while also clearing the trunk lid. Though the luggage space acccess was never considered, the wing's height happily checked that issue off the list of problems the Charger Daytona could've had.
Homologation rules only forced Dodge to build 503 examples of the 1969 Charger Daytona for showroom duty, comprising 433 cars equipped with the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) Magnum V8 and a mere 70 packing the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi V8. Plymouth followed suit for the 1970 season with 1,935 Road Runner Superbirds, including 135 Hemi cars, before NASCAR banned the aero warriors into oblivion. Meanwhile, Dodge finally remembered that compact pony cars existed.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 Arriving fashionably dead last to the pony car brawl on September 25, 1969, the 1970 Dodge Challenger stretched its E-body wheelbase 2 inches (51 millimeters) beyond the Plymouth Barracuda while sharing nada exterior body panels with its sibling. Across five model years from 1970 through 1974, U.S. production reached 165,437 units, with 76,935 for 1970 alone. Then the whole fashion went really South really fast: 26,299 for 1971, 22,919 for 1972, 27,930 for 1973, and 11,354 before ending in April 1974.
To compensate for showing up late, Dodge stuffed everything from docile 225-cubic-inch (3.7-liter) Slant Six-cylinder engines to the earth-shattering 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi V8 rated at 425 horsepower (431 PS) under the Challenger hood. Out of 18,512 Challenger R/T models built for 1970, only 356 received the Hemi, including 287 hardtops, 60 Special Edition coupes, and nine convertibles, with 154 featuring automatic transmissions, before Hemi production plunged to 71 cars for 1971.
This particular R-code heavyweight rolled off the Hamtramck, Michigan assembly line in November 1969 as 1 of only 150 non-SE 1970 Hemi Challenger R/T hardtops fitted with the 3-speed TorqueFlite automatic. Verified by its original broadcast sheet, fender tag, and core support stamping JS23R0B193316, the coupe wore Go Mango paint alongside the 426 Hemi, a Performance Axle Package, and California emissions equipment.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 When the original buyer bought the beast in July 1970 through a military credit union, dealership mechanics indulged his glorious lack of restraint by bolting a genuine 1969 Charger Daytona wing directly onto the rear quarters. Using four bolts per upright and zero internal trunk braces, that installation risked buckling the sheet metal at high speed. Vintage Polaroids found inside the trunk confirm it wore that wing from day 1.
Even the California Department of Motor Vehicles joined the comedy routine by issuing sequential 1970 blue license plates reading 426 BPW, accidentally matching the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) elephant under the hood. Naturally, owning a winged Hemi Challenger with a "426" plate demanded immediate high-speed validation, including a fabled dealership-backed run on the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah, where the original factory engine promptly celebrated its freedom by grenading itself in 1970.
Because the mechanical fireworks happened while the car was still fresh off the lot, Chrysler graciously supplied a hydraulic-lifter warranty replacement 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi block carrying a riveted teal tag and factory broach marks stamped only with T and A. Although a dark blue oil pan sparked rumors of a marine engine, Bergeron proved the block was unpainted factory iron topped by its original $3,500-apiece dual 4-barrel Carter AFB carburetors.
Photo: YouTube/DezzysSpeedShop As if the towering Dodge Scat Pack Club wing and "426 Hemi 660" hood emblems were too subtle, someone slapped a 200 mph (322 kph) decal over the 160 mph (257 kph) Rallye speedometer, which reads 3,942 miles (6,344 kilometers) despite an estimated 30,000 miles (48,280 kilometers) traveled. Inside, the working key buzzer, Rim Blow wheel, and 1990s black-and-orange upholstery complement an older pearl-tinted orange respray, window louvers, and California exhaust turndowns.
The original owner treasured his winged anomaly for 49 years until chemotherapy forced a sale to a close friend in 2019, complete with unmounted tires dated August 2005 stacked inside his kitchen. Over the next several years, the second caretaker drove it barely 10 miles (16 kilometers) due to mushy drum brakes, while a $1,200 recore needed for its 956 radiator, $50 hourly shop rates, and steep pricing deterred Bergeron.
After having just 2 owners across 56 years, the rust-free survivor retaining its factory Hemi torque boxes and collapsible spare tire suddenly became the hottest ticket on the market. Purchased on August 14, 2026, and flipped again on August 20, 2026, the coupe doubled its ownership roll call in 5.6 days before heading toward Ohio, standing forever as hilarious proof that in 1970, one could order their car exactly as they wanted it.

2026 SEMA Show • Stellantis Uses Direct Connection to Unleash No Less Than Six New HEMI V8 Crate Engine Packages
2028 Chevrolet Tahoe and Suburban Switch to the Fifth and Thirteenth Generations, Though Only in CGI
19 photos
Photo: AutoYa Interior / YouTube
General Motors has great things for Chevrolet and GMC going on, like the all-new 2027 Silverado and Sierra 1500 pickup truck generations, the all-new Mongoose 8.3-liter Duramax diesel for the HD versions, and hybrid power coming to some of the most popular large SUVs.
Chevrolet first revealed the next-generation Silverado 1500 earlier this year during the first month of summer, and a few days later the latest iteration of the Sierra 1500 from GMC was also made official. They share their underpinnings, as always, and also the full exterior and interior redesigns, along with four powertrain options – the more potent 2.7-liter TurboMax four-pot along with the 3.0-liter Duramax diesel engines are carried over, and all powertrains now feature a ten-speed automatic transmission.
But there are also major novelties – the fresh 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter small-block V8s. The HD fans weren’t left in the dark, because the heavy-duty gained a fresh 8.3-liter Duramax ‘ Mongoose ’ diesel made to combat the Ford Super Duty and the Ram HD. Also, GM is allegedly spending no less than $750 million to electrify some of its largest SUVs, the Chevy Traverse plus Buick Enclave as well as the GMC Acadia. Now, the rumor mill is also shifting its attention to the biggest Chevy SUVs – the Tahoe and Suburban.
More precisely, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have a satellite " AutoYa Interior " venue which unofficially imagined the CGI look of the potentially all-new 2028 Chevy Tahoe full-size SUV, as the channel’s host believes that next year, we’ll get to see the next generations for both the Tahoe and Suburban, complete with exterior and interior changes along with new powertrain options.
The most logical course of action would be to assume that both the Chevy Tahoe and Suburban will follow closely in the footsteps of the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and get the same powertrain options, including GM’s brand-new V8s. It would also be nice to envision the larger Suburban with the Mongoose under the hood, but that’s probably just stretching it.
Anyway, the channel’s resident member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators has stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI and opted to illustrate the potential look of the 2028 Chevy Tahoe in their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project, both inside and outside. This could also become a second facelift for the big SUVs, though, as the changes aren’t numerous.
We can see at the front a new split-headlight redesign with a full-width LED bar and new headlights plus a redesigned bumper, but the profile is left exactly the same, and around the back only the LED taillights are modified. The situation is even subtler inside, where the changes are mostly minor across the board. On the other hand, the traditional color reel rocks a ton of ritzy colors, both inside and outside, and from many viewing angles.

2026 SEMA Show • Ford Frostwarden, a Bronco SUV With Over 1,200 HP, the R125 and F-250 Also in Tow
Holy-Grail 1970 Plymouth Hemi Cuda Convertible Hits the Block, One of Only 5 Made
14 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Redesigned and built on a brand-new platform, the 1970 Plymouth Barracuda sold nearly 49,000 units. It was the nameplate's best year since 1967. About a third of these cars were ordered as performance Cuda models, and only half of the Cudas were equipped with big-block V8 powerplants.
About 4,800 were equipped with the standard 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8. The remaining units were ordered with the more iconic 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) RB and 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi. The four-barrel 440 found its way into 986 cars, while the six-barrel version was fitted into 1,784 examples.
The 426 Hemi V8 is the rarest of the Cuda bunch, which 666 units made. But you know which Cuda is actually much rarer? The Cuda convertible. This applies to all drop tops, regardless of the engine, but things became ultra scarce when there's a Hemi convertible combo.
Drop-top sales were low across the entire American auto industry in 1970. Plymouth received only 2,501 orders for the convertible version, including all three trim levels. The Cuda is the scarcest, with only examples sold. How many got the 425-horsepower Hemi engine ? Only 14!
Of these, nine were fitted with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic transmission, while the other five received the four-speed manual gearbox. It's unclear how many of these cars are still around, but I can tell you that they rarely pop up at public events. Likewise, they rarely go under the hammer.
If you haven't seen one recently, a four-speed drop-top Hemi was just included among the lots scheduled to go under the hammer at Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction in January. And it's quite a spectacular sight.
In addition to the rare and highly desirable drivetrain combo, this Cuda also sports Mopar's iconic metallic purple paint. I'm obviously talking about In-Violet (Plum Crazy on Dodge models), one of the 10 high-impact colors offered between 1969 and 1973. In-Violet was only available in 1970 and 1971.
There's no info on whether the 12,000-mile (19,312 km) reading on the odometer is authentic, but I have a feeling it was reset during the restoration. Yes, this Cuda underwent a frame-off refresh, which was so outstanding that it brought it a MCACN Concours Gold award back in 2015. Needless to say, the Mopar still looks flawless some 11 years later.
The options list reveals that this Cuda rolled off the assembly line with the A34 Super Track Pak. The bundle includes a Sure Grip rear end with 4.10 gears. Of course, it also has all the goodies you can expect to find on a Hemi Cuda , including the Shaker hood, tie-down pins, the 26-inch radiator, and the heavy-duty suspension.
How much will this stunning Mopar change hands for? Well, it should sell for a seven-figure sum. The rare drop-tops are usually appraised at over $1 million, but two cars were traded for over $2 million in recent years. Will this In-Violet example set a new record? We will find out on January 16.

2026 SEMA Show • This Batmobile-Looking Lamborghini Temerario Is on Display at SEMA
Cheapest CGI Audi Q9 Has Plastic Bumpers, Black Steelies, Manual Tranny, Cloth Seats, Analog Dials
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
Audi has gone down in preferences for the American customers over the past few months – the sales are showing a 15% drop during the third quarter of the year and an even higher 16% slide year-to-date, after nine months.
The problem is that Audi didn’t sign off on 2025 as a record year and didn’t even have a positive outlook. But no worries, as the company has faith in its North American operations thanks to the introduction of brand-new models like the A5 and A6 series, which surged 21% and 24% during the nine months, and also just started selling the all-new Q7 along with the first-ever Q9 full-size three-row crossover SUV.
The latter two will probably impact the charts beginning with next year after they ramp up across dealerships, but Audi wants even more – they announced at the end of October 2026 a long-term commitment with a massive US production site in Georgia worth about $4 billion and some 4,500 new jobs. It will focus, beginning in 2030, on its premium “SUVs tailored to North American customers,” which most likely means the likes of Audi’s Q7 and Q9 will have a second home alongside the Volkswagen Bratislava Plant in Slovakia.
Currently, the all-new 2027 Audi Q7 and the larger Q9 are starting at $70,900 for the Q7, $98,700 for the SQ7, and $87,700 or $118k for the Q9 and SQ9, respectively. That’s a lot of cash and nobody can promise that once they are getting made locally the prices will go down – inflation tends to erode these expectations. So, what’s the solution for a more accessible Audi Q9, for example?
Well, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular has a proposition in his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project. More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the new 2027 Audi Q9 SUV and make it part of his new CGI Pure Stock series.
He previously worked on models like the Mercedes- AMG GT SUV , Jaguar Type 01, G50 BMW 3 Series, Bentley Torcal, or the G65 BMW X5, among others. There was also a CGI Pure Stock 2027 Audi Q7, so, of course, now it’s also the ripe time for the same CGI treatment to be applied to the larger 2027 Audi Q9.
The base 2027 Audi Q9, in his vision, comes dressed in non-metallic white, which is now the default free color for many brands, and also has a black plastic grille, black roof rails, black window surrounds, black mirror caps, black door handles, along with black bumpers, side sills, and fender surrounds. At least we’re left with the front and rear LED lights and the color-matching roof spoiler.
Inside, the stock Q9 would make any classic SUV enthusiast blush with excitement: gone is the triple-screen setup and the fancy leather upholstery. In their place now resides a completely different cockpit experience. More precisely, the pixel master has opted for classic round-dial Audi analog instruments for the driver’s cluster, a bezel-heavy and small central screen, separate manual climate controls, and a six-speed manual transmission plus cloth upholstery.
There’s even a manual handbrake lever, as well as what looks like recycled materials on the door cards. What do you think – yay or nay? Would you buy something like this? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)
